summary: Adolf Noreen was a linguist who studied at Uppsala University (~1871–1877) and under August Leskien (~1879). He held a post at Uppsala University from around 1877 to 1919.

Adolf Schlagintweit was an explorer and historian who earned his Dr.med. at the University of Munich (~1846–1849). He served as a Privatdozent at Munich in 1850 and was employed by the East India Company for exploration in 1854.

Adolf Tobler was a linguist who studied at the University of Zurich and the University of Bonn under Friedrich Christian Diez and Nikolaus Delius (~1854–1856). He held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin from 1867 to 1910.

Indologist and linguist Adolfo Esteller y Melià earned doctorates at the Pontifical Gregorian University and Humboldt University of Berlin. He later served as professor at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1937–1964) and director of the Heras Institute (1956–1963).
Linguist Adolphe Pictet studied at Geneva, Paris, Edinburgh, London, and Humboldt University of Berlin under G. W. F. Hegel. He served as a Privatdozent at the University of Geneva from 1840 to 1844.

Adolphe Regnier worked in Indology, linguistics, and history, studying under Eugène Burnouf. He held posts at Lycée Saint-Louis, Lycée Charlemagne, Collège de France, École Normale Supérieure, the Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres, and the Palace of Fontainebleau.

Adoniram Judson Eaton was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Acadia, Harvard, Yale, and Leipzig (Ph.D. ~1882–1884). He held posts at Amherst Academy, Woonsocket High School, and McGill University.

Indologist Adriaan Scharpé earned doctorates from KU Leuven and Utrecht University, studying under Albert Joseph Carnoy and Jan Gonda. He held faculty posts at Ghent University (1944–1979) and the University of Amsterdam (1947–1978).

Adrian Zenz specializes in Tibetology and Sinology. Educated at the University of Auckland and the University of Cambridge, he has held posts at the European School of Culture and Theology, Columbia International University Korntal, and the Victims of Communism Memorial Foundation.
Linguist Adrien Barthélemy studied Iranian and Central Asian subjects at INALCO and EPHE under James Darmesteter. From 1909 to 1929, he taught at INALCO and served as directeur d’études at EPHE.

Adrienne Audrey G. Bennett worked in Buddhist and religious studies. She served as librarian at the Buddhist Society (1949–1952), editor for The Middle Way (1951–1952), and held a post at the Maha Bodhi Society (1956–1966).

Adrián Muñoz works in Indology and religious studies. He has held posts as an Associate Professor of Comparative Religion at UNAM (attested 2011) and as a lecturer of South Asian Religions at El Colegio de México (attested 2020).

Afeef Ahmed is a scholar of Indology and history who has held a post at the Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar. He became a graduate student and Ph.D. candidate in South Asian Studies at Harvard University.

Agata Bareja-Starzyńska is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Central Asian studies. She conducted research at the University of Oslo and University of Bonn, and held posts at the University of Warsaw attested in 2008 and 2026.
Agathe Keller is a scholar of Indology and history who earned her PhD and Habilitation at Paris Diderot University in 2000. She has held posts at REHSEIS, Paris Diderot University, and the CNRS.

Indologist Agehananda Bharati studied at the University of Vienna and Sannyasi Mahavidyalaya. He held teaching posts at Delhi, Banaras Hindu University, Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, Mahamakut Buddhist University, Tokyo, Kyoto, the University of Washington, and Syracuse University (1961–1991).
Agnes Margrethe Agerschou was an Indologist and linguist who completed her M.A. at the University of Copenhagen in 1940. She worked as an assistant for the Critical Pāli Dictionary from 1940 to 1949.

Agnieszka Helman-Ważny specializes in Tibetology and history. Educated at the Academy of Fine Arts in Warsaw and Nicolaus Copernicus University, she has held posts at Cornell University, the University of Hamburg, and the University of Warsaw.

Agvan Dorzhiev was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who earned the Geshey Lharampa degree at Drepung Monastery (Drepung Gomang Dratsang). He founded Atsagat Datsan in 1913 and Datsan Gunzechoinei.

Ahmad Hasan Dani was a historian and Indologist who studied at Banaras Hindu University and the University of London. He held main posts at the University of Dhaka, the University of Peshawar, and Quaid-i-Azam University.
